rules.description: Strong masculine: uninflected nominative/accusative singular, -es/-e; plural -as/-a/-um/-as.
Retain the vowel in the final short-stem element sceamul before endings; the long first element fōt- does not turn the final element into a heavy stem. Full uncontracted cells selected.
Heavy neuter nominative/accusative singular and plural have no ending; other endings -es/-e/-a/-um. Short final stem bebod- takes plural -u.
hēafod has the syncopated hēafd- stem before endings, with selected nominative/accusative plural hēafdu (§47.1,6).

Heavy feminine: nominative singular uninflected; oblique singular -e; plural -a/-a/-um/-a. -nes doubles s before endings. Abstract -ung/-ing has the same selected endings; -a oblique singular variants remain recognition alternatives.
Weak masculine: -a nominative singular, -an other singular and nominative/accusative plural, -ena genitive plural, -um dative plural.
tōð follows fōt: dative singular and nominative/accusative plural tēð, genitive singular tōðes, plural genitive tōða and dative tōðum. Cook also admits tōðe and tōðas.

bōc: genitive/dative singular and nominative/accusative plural bēc; genitive plural bōca, dative plural bōcum. Genitive singular bōce follows the explicitly admitted regular -e genitive alternative for this class.
sweostor is unchanged throughout the singular and nominative/accusative plural, with genitive plural sweostra and dative plural sweostrum; no invented umlaut.

Selected people names Engle and Dęne have plural-only lexical scope: -e nominative/accusative, -a genitive, -um dative. Dęniga/Dęnia genitive plural variants are explicit in §44.2; do not manufacture a singular by backformation.
Agent noun in -end: selected plural nominative/accusative zero, genitive -ra, dative -um. Cook admits nominative/accusative plural -e and -as variants.

Complete singular selection hǣtu/hǣte and invariant hǣlu; -u/-o/-e oblique variation is recognized. Wright184 §§382–383 explicitly lists both under strengu and warns few such nouns have plurals. BT500b lists hǣlu indeclinable. No plural lexical use assigned.

Wright184 prints the complete strengu class model: singular nominative strengu/-o, accusative/genitive/dative strenge/-u/-o; plural nominative/accusative strenga/-e/-u/-o, genitive strenga and dative strengum. Select one explicit eight-cell reference column without assigning an independently productive count sense. Earlier ðīestru taught only plural forms and does not establish this complete class.

rules.statement: Ne precedes a finite verb. The selected negative copula combines uncontracted ne eom/ne eart/ne sindon with nis and the contracted preterite næs/nǣre/nǣron. These alternatives form one complete twelve-position indicative construction table. An uncontracted cell contains two existing words, not a new multiword inflected verb. Negative willan selects Cook’s e-vowel alternatives nelle/nelt/nele/nellað and nolde/noldest/noldon. Other spellings are valid source variants, not extra selected recall targets.

Cook’s habban table and ne+h contraction (§29), with the already checked Unit2 negative cells, give næbbe, næfst, næfð, nabbað; preterite næfde, næfdest, næfde, næfdon. The negative cells are rule-derived, not separately printed in a full negative table. Do not conflate first-singular bb with other singular f. Retain the earlier form identities and recognition histories.

Nān follows strong long-stem adjective NGDA endings, with nominative/accusative neuter plural nān and feminine plural nāna, masculine accusative singular nānne. Long ā remains. No invented weak system or general negative spelling rule.
Gehwā compounds the singular interrogative hwā/hwæt. Select prior gehwǣm (not silently substitute hwām). Accusative persons gehwone versus things gehwæt. No distinct feminine morphology or plural.
The selected adverb has swīðe, swīðor, swīðost, with unchanged long ī. The comparative can mark preference with ðonne; the two compared objects retain their governed case.

StrongIII forgieldan has present gield-, past singular geald-, plural guld-, participle gold-. Present2/3 forgieltst/forgielt continue the earlier gieldan selected t cluster. Tōweorpan has weorp-/wearp-/wurp-/worpen; its present2/3 uses umlaut wierp-. Past2singular uses the plural stem plus -e. Singular1/3past bare stem; all pastpl -on. All presentpl -að. Prefixes stay with all stems.

Ongietan follows gietan/giefan classV: ongiet-/ongeat-/ongēat-/ongieten. Present2 ongietst and3 ongiett keep selected t+t assimilation (Cook prints giet(t)); the alternative single t is valid but not the selected cell. Preterite2 uses ongēate, other singular ongeat, plural ongēaton. The infinitive and participle in the principal-parts display are reference only.

Gehātan follows the prior hātan selected system with ge-: gehāte/gehǣtst/gehǣtt/gehātað; past gehēt/gehēte/gehēton. The ā→ǣ present2/3 and ēpast are both required. Onfōn keeps the contract infinitives onfōn/onfōnne; forlǣtan keeps forlǣtan/forlǣtanne. No negative or subjunctive prefixed system is inferred.

Standan is classVI, not classIII: standan/stōd/stōdon/standen. Its present base standende keeps the nasal in the present stem; past standen is the selected fourth principal part. Only the participial base pair is newly promoted.

Selected long-stem weakI wēnan,lǣran,forbærnan use present -e,-st,-ð,-að and preterite -de,-dest,-de,-don. Selected participial bases lǣrende/lǣred and hǣlende/hǣled retain full -ed; the frame does not license arbitrary syncopation. Imperative singular has no ending (ætīew, ālīes); plural -að. Plain/inflected wyrcean/wyrceanne preserve earlier selected -ea- before the infinitival ending, rather than silently substituting wyrcan.

Weak II hȳrian follows lufian: present hȳrie, hȳrast, hȳrað, hȳriað; preterite hȳrode, hȳrodest, hȳrode, hȳrodon. The long ȳ is lexical and stays throughout. Commands cleopa/cleopiað distinguish singular -a from plural -iað. The selected pair is blōstmian/blōstmianne; no finite system is assigned.

Riht and gelīc use ordinary long-stem positive adjective NGDA endings. Zero nominative feminine singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural; strong feminine plural -a selected, masculine -e; weak genitive plural -ra. Long ī in gelīc stays.

Mǣre is Cook§59: retain citation -e where no ending is supplied; drop it before another ending, including selected feminine nominative singular mǣru and neuter nominative/accusative plural mǣru. Strong -re/-ra with stem-final r contracts to mǣrre/mǣrra. Weak genitive plural mǣrra.

Mihtig follows the disyllabic -ig pattern (§57.3): the selected table syncopates i before vowel-initial endings (mihtges, mihtgum, mihtge, mihtgan); retains i before consonantal endings (mihtigne, mihtigre, mihtigra). Select mihtig for strong feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural, parallel to the established hālig pattern. Unsyncopated variants must not be called impossible.

Ungeðancfull is explicitly Cook§58.2: retain final ll before vowels (ungeðancfulle, -fullum), but select one l before consonants (ungeðancfulne, -fulre, -fulra). Bare ungeðancfull keeps the lexical double consonant.

scope_note: Every lexical diagnostic and exception must accompany the matching literal table. Complete morphology is not a blanket assignment of syntax or count senses.
